title: How Far Will the Canada-EU Lovefest Go?
gist: Von der Leyen's idea of EU 'associate membership' for Canada has no treaty basis, but Ottawa and Brussels are deepening ties beyond CETA — into critical minerals, AI, energy, defense (SAFE) and digital trade — as both diversify away from Trump's America. Bechev argues formal membership is off the table near-term, but an EEA- or post-Brexit-style model could emerge if the EU embraces 'flexible geometry' with its many non-member partners.

themes.theme: Associate membership: slogan vs. legal reality

insights.claim: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen floated associate EU membership for Canada, but no such status exists in the EU's founding treaties; Article 217 'association' agreements underpin ties with aspiring members, whereas Canada's CETA rests on the EU's commercial-policy article.
insights.speaker: Dimitar Bechev
insights.so_what: Headlines about Canada 'joining' the EU overstate near-term change; real integration will come via sectoral agreements.
